q: How big is the main pump track at Flight Deck?
a: 25,000 square feet of Velosolutions asphalt — the largest Velosolutions pump track in Southern California. The track is designed for progression, so beginners can ride the gentler rollers while advanced riders use the larger features.

q: Is Flight Deck suitable for adaptive riders and beginners?
a: Yes. The facility includes the region's first adaptive track (designed for riders of all abilities), an asphalt bicycle playground for young riders just getting started, and a main pump track built for every skill level. The connecting AGT path is also ADA-accessible.

q: What is the Ambient Glow Technology (AGT) path?
a: A 1,000-foot connecting path uses Ambient Glow Technology — sunlight-charged glow rocks that illuminate the trail after dark. Per the City, this is the first use of this technology in Southern California.

q: What's the design story behind the Flight Deck name?
a: Per the City, the park was inspired by Moreno Valley's aviation heritage and was designed to offer a welcoming cycling experience for riders of all ages, abilities, and skill levels. It was designed and built by American Ramp Company.

q: What can I ride at Flight Deck?
a: Bikes, standard non-motorized scooters, skateboards, and rollerblades are welcome. Motorized bikes and motorized scooters are strictly prohibited.

13460 Morrison Street, on the southern side of Morrison Park near the Fire Station. The 2.5-acre facility is part of the larger 35-acre Morrison Park campus — see Morrison Park for ballfields, picnic shelters, and other amenities.

q: Does Flight Deck cost anything to enter?
a: No — admission is free, like the rest of Morrison Park. Open daily 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM.
